prompt: Create original cartoon 2D game terrain source artwork, NOT a poster, NOT a rendered 3D object, NOT pixel art. One single broad horizontal repeatable cliff-front strip, viewed straight-on from a slightly elevated orthographic RPG camera. Flat horizontal upper boundary, flat lower contact baseline; left and right edges are straight cut-through boundaries intended to meet another strip, NOT closed end caps and NOT tapered inward. Five logical cells wide. A shallow plain muted spring-green plateau surface across the top, roughly one quarter of the strip height, then a vertical cool grey granite cliff face across the remaining three quarters. Natural large interlocking granite formations with varied sizes and irregular fractures, broad simple hand-painted/cel-shaded color regions, clean confident dark grey outlines, gentle upper-left lighting. Avoid repeating stacks of identical stones, masonry bricks, noisy photoreal detail, triangulated low-poly surfaces, extreme cracks, grass tufts, flowers, loose props and moss decoration. Grass meets stone with a thin irregular soil seam and occasional exposed rock, never a thick floating turf slab. Keep the plain green surface compatible with a calm light meadow-green ground texture. The artwork should be a useful modular terrain source rather than a complete island/platform or a scenic illustration. Center the one long strip in a wide landscape canvas with solid exact chroma green #00FF00 everywhere outside the strip. No transparency, checkerboards, gradients in the background, shadows outside the silhouette, drawn grid lines, labels, text, borders, water, waterfall, buildings or characters. Strip takes about 90 percent of canvas width and 45 percent of canvas height, leaving clean green margins all around. Grass color distinctly less saturated than the chroma green. Maintain a level top and bottom so the source can be calibrated for a 64-game-pixel vertical rise with a separately measured plateau footprint. Do not create extra rows or extra disconnected samples.
